B. Whether prestige attached to the cook is doing the work attributed to culinary criteria.
C. Whether the visitor necessarily invented the dish.
D. Whether regional cooks are unable to change a recipe.
normal.explain: 在未提出做法差異時，評價轉變可能依名望而非宣稱的料理標準；並未證明動機。

normal.desc: 【語用】The review praises the restaurant’s refusal to sentimentalise its origins, then faults it for failing to reproduce the reviewer’s remembered childhood. What inconsistency emerges?
options: A. It supplies evidence that the reviewer had no childhood connection.
B. It proves that the restaurant has concealed its origins.
C. It commends independence from nostalgia while imposing a nostalgic benchmark.
D. It consistently rejects all personal memory as irrelevant.
normal.explain: 先讚不感傷追憶，又以童年回憶要求重現，判準有張力。

normal.desc: 請唸出單字：滋味鮮明而略帶刺激感的
請唸出單字：使口腔感到收斂乾澀的
請唸出：對細節極其講究的關注
請唸出：與整體不相稱的華麗點綴
請唸出：名望可能代替了宣稱由品味所作的判斷
normal.ans: PRESTIGE MAY BE DOING THE WORK ATTRIBUTED TO TASTE
normal.speak: prestige may be doing the work attributed to taste
normal.vocabId: R8:PRESTIGE MAY BE DOING THE WORK ATTRIBUTED TO TASTE

normal.desc: 請唸出：解說幾乎不留自主感受的空間
normal.ans: THE EXPLANATION LEAVES LITTLE ROOM FOR AN UNPRESCRIBED RESPONSE
normal.speak: the explanation leaves little room for an unprescribed response
normal.vocabId: R8:THE EXPLANATION LEAVES LITTLE ROOM FOR AN UNPRESCRIBED RESPONSE

normal.desc: 請拼出：甜味或濃郁程度過頭而令人膩的（C 開頭，7 個字母）
請拼出：食物淡而乏味的（I 開頭，7 個字母）
請拼出：豪華而豐盛的（S 開頭，9 個字母）
填空題：E P I _ U R E (講究並欣賞精緻飲食的人)
填空題：G U S _ A T _ R Y (與味覺有關的)
填空題：R _ P _ _ T (一頓餐食的正式或文學說法)
🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
options: A. 經多次獨立確認的穩定結論
B. 可永久保存的實體標本
C. 刻意逐字複製的文字
D. 很快消逝而難以留住的印象
normal.explain: evanescent 指短暫而很快消失，偏正式文學語域。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
options: A. 可能犯錯的觀察者
B. 故意造假的觀察者
C. 從不可能犯錯的觀察者
D. 完全無法接收感官資訊的人
normal.explain: fallible 是會犯錯，不包含故意欺騙。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
options: A. 所有觀察者同時撤回的紀錄
B. 與預期模式不符的目擊
C. 已被定義為典型的目擊
D. 完全沒有發生的目擊
normal.explain: anomalous 指異於常態，不自動代表虛假。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
options: A. 可知或可證成程度的限制
B. 只能攜帶一件行李的限制
C. 通往觀察地點的路障
D. 儀器的外觀尺寸
normal.explain: epistemic 是關於知識，不是物流或物理尺寸。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
normal.speak: The account is not implausible; it is simply more determinate than the observations warrant.
options: A. 說話者只嫌描述字數不足。
B. 說明並非不合理，只是比觀察足以支持的更為確定。
C. 說明已被判定不可能且完全荒謬。
D. 觀察已唯一確定每個細節。
normal.explain: 接受可能性，同時批評定論程度過高。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
normal.speak: The observer’s candour about uncertainty makes the record more trustworthy, without making the identification any less provisional.
options: A. 暫定辨識表示紀錄必定不誠實。
B. 紀錄可信就不需要任何佐證。
C. 坦承不確定讓紀錄較可信，但辨識仍是暫定。
D. 誠實已使辨識成為不可修正的事實。
normal.explain: 來源誠實度與分類確定度可分開評價。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
normal.speak: To describe the boundary as natural is already to interpret the pattern, not merely to reproduce it.
options: A. 重現圖案與理解圖案被定義為相同。
B. 稱界線為自然形成，已在解釋模式，而非只是重現。
C. 自然一詞不可能包含任何解釋。
D. 說話者確認所有界線都是人為製造。
normal.explain: 指出描述語言含解釋，不據此斷言界線必然人造。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
normal.speak: The elegance of the account lies in what it unifies; its vulnerability lies in how readily inconvenient cases become exceptions to be explained away.
options: A. 說明善於處理不符案例，弱點只在未能提出統整架構。
B. 說明承認例外過多，因此作者已決定放棄整個統整架構。
C. 說明能統整現象，但太容易藉例外消解不符案例的挑戰。
D. 說明雖有不符案例，仍因統整優雅而已排除所有重要弱點。
normal.explain: 兼評統整價值與排除反例的風險；explain away 有消解質疑之意。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
normal.speak: What the report calls independent confirmation is not wholly independent of the expectations that determined where its observers stood.
options: A. 所謂獨立確認是指不同觀察者曾站在相同位置。
B. 搜尋位置雖受預期影響，紀錄量已排除這種影響。
C. 搜尋位置與預期一致，已構成另一份獨立確認。
D. 所謂獨立確認仍受決定搜尋位置的預期影響。
normal.explain: 資料取得受預期引導，質疑獨立性，不等於全部無效。

normal.desc: 【語意】The report’s apparent precision belies the uncertainty of its underlying categories. What does belies indicate?
options: A. The precise appearance openly explains every uncertainty.
B. The categories have been proved unnecessary.
C. The figures are explicitly rounded to avoid any precision.
D. The precise appearance gives a misleading impression of what supports it.
normal.explain: belies 指表象未如實呈現；此處精確外表掩飾分類不確定性。

normal.desc: 【文法】Were the same search conducted at night, its findings ___ substantially.
options: A. might differ
B. had differing
C. might to differ
D. would have differ
normal.explain: Were ... conducted 是假設條件倒裝，主句用 might + 原形。

normal.desc: 【語意】The account is scrupulous about distinguishing observation from inference. What is praised?
options: A. Its certainty that the distinction has no practical value.
B. Its careful adherence to that distinction.
C. Its refusal to offer any interpretation at all.
D. Its preference for elaborate descriptions over accurate ones.
normal.explain: scrupulous 指嚴謹細心遵循，不等於全面拒絕推論。

normal.desc: 【範圍】The species is elusive, not necessarily scarce. What distinction is preserved?
options: A. Difficulty of detection does not by itself establish low abundance.
B. Every elusive animal must be abundant.
C. Scarcity makes detection impossible in principle.
D. The species has been identified incorrectly.
normal.explain: elusive 難發現，scarce 數量稀少，兩者不等同。

normal.desc: 【修辭】The report treats the map’s blank spaces as though nature, rather than the survey, had left them empty. What is the criticism?
options: A. Natural features cannot be represented on a map.
B. A gap in observation is being presented as a property of the observed world.
C. The map has been printed with insufficient ink.
D. The survey explicitly marks every blank as uncertain.
normal.explain: 反諷把認知上的空白實體化為自然界不存在。

normal.desc: 【文法】The conclusion depends on a distinction, the stability ___ the report never examines.
options: A. that of
B. which of
C. of which
D. of whose
normal.explain: the stability of which 為關係子句結構，which 指 distinction。

normal.desc: 【立場】The critic objects less to the categories themselves than to their being mistaken for self-evident divisions in nature. What is the objection?
options: A. Nature has been proved to contain no differences.
B. A useful classification is being treated as if its boundaries needed no justification.
C. All classification is said to be impossible and pointless.
D. The categories have not been used in the report.
normal.explain: less ... than ... 將批評對準把分類自然化，非廢除分類。

normal.desc: 【短文】Surveyors search intensively where a model predicts a species, then cite the concentration of sightings in those areas as independent confirmation of the model. Which issue requires scrutiny?
options: A. The confirmation would be independent if more observers used the same plan.
B. The confirmation shows the model caused the species to favour those areas.
C. The confirmation may partly reflect a search pattern shaped by the model.
D. The confirmation is weakened because the observed animals moved too often.
normal.explain: 證據的生成受被驗模型引導，獨立性不足；不否定目擊真實性。

normal.desc: 【短文】A report acknowledges uncertainty in every individual record but presents the combined total without qualification. No account is given of how the uncertainties interact. What is missing?
options: A. An account of why combining records necessarily increases uncertainty.
B. A demonstration that every individual record concerns a different species.
C. A demonstration that the number of records exceeds the number of observers.
D. An account of how the individual uncertainties affect the combined total.
normal.explain: 聚合可能增減不確定，需說明機制；不能自動抹除或斷言必然線性增加。

normal.desc: 請唸出單字：短暫而迅速消逝的
請唸出單字：關於知識及其可證成程度的
請唸出：難以納入解釋的頑強反例
請唸出：在方法上審慎而不過度推論的結論
請唸出：誠實觀察者仍可能辨識錯誤
normal.ans: AN HONEST OBSERVER MAY STILL MAKE A MISTAKEN IDENTIFICATION
normal.speak: an honest observer may still make a mistaken identification
normal.vocabId: R8:AN HONEST OBSERVER MAY STILL MAKE A MISTAKEN IDENTIFICATION

normal.desc: 請唸出：建構的分類不必是任意的
normal.ans: A CONSTRUCTED CATEGORY NEED NOT BE AN ARBITRARY ONE
normal.speak: a constructed category need not be an arbitrary one
normal.vocabId: R8:A CONSTRUCTED CATEGORY NEED NOT BE AN ARBITRARY ONE

normal.desc: 請拼出：可能犯錯而非絕對可靠的（F 開頭，8 個字母）
請拼出：嚴謹細心而恪守標準的（S 開頭，10 個字母）
請拼出：將抽象概念視為具體實體的做法（R 開頭，11 個字母）
填空題：E L U _ I V E (難以找到辨認或掌握的)
填空題：A N O _ A L _ U S (不符合通常模式或預期的)
填空題：C I _ C U _ S P _ C T (仔細考量而審慎的)
🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
options: A. 令人蒙羞的失敗
B. 雖敗猶榮的結果
C. 不分勝負的平手
D. 未經爭奪的勝利
normal.explain: ignominious 帶羞辱不光彩，非僅分差大小。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
options: A. 要求敗者承擔獎盃費用
B. 獲勝後對敗者寬厚大方
C. 獲勝後反覆羞辱敗者
D. 因不確定獲勝而拒絕慶祝
normal.explain: magnanimous 指寬宏大度，尤其面對對手。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
options: A. 熱烈鼓勵對手的反應
B. 僅以書面提出的回應
C. 無禮而欠缺大方的反應
D. 謹慎而不失體諒的反應
normal.explain: churlish 指粗魯小氣，不是正式書面語域。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
options: A. 只因過於簡短而無法理解的句子
B. 貌似有理卻站不住腳的辯解
C. 經獨立查核而成立的理由
D. 坦白承認沒有理由的表態
normal.explain: specious 指表面可信但實質不成立。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
normal.speak: The apology was punctilious about etiquette and curiously evasive about the conduct that had made an apology necessary.
options: A. 說話者因道歉禮貌而認為已充分交代行為。
B. 道歉的問題只在於使用了過多正式稱謂。
C. 道歉對禮節一絲不苟，對導致需道歉的行為卻迴避。
D. 道歉詳細承認行為，但對禮節顯得粗魯隨便。
normal.explain: 程序禮數與承擔實質行為責任不同。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
normal.speak: His equanimity is admirable, though the commentators seem determined to make it evidence that the defeat did not hurt.
options: A. 他的鎮定已充分證實他對失敗毫無情緒。
B. 評論者拒絕承認他在失敗後保持鎮定。
C. 說話者認為在意輸贏就不可能有任何自制。
D. 他的鎮定值得欣賞，但評論者硬把它當成失敗不令他難過的證據。
normal.explain: 外在平靜不直接證明內在不痛苦。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
normal.speak: The rivalry gives the event its energy; the mythology of mutual hatred is largely a promotional embellishment.
options: A. 競爭本身是宣傳捏造，雙方從未交手。
B. 說話者認為只要宣傳就能讓雙方真正敵視。
C. 競爭帶來活力；彼此仇恨的傳說多半是宣傳加油添醋。
D. 彼此仇恨已被確認是活動活力的唯一來源。
normal.explain: 承認 rivalry，區分其與宣傳誇大的 hatred。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
normal.speak: It is a peculiar meritocracy that treats the advantages required to enter the contest as though they were achievements secured by winning it.
options: A. 這種唯才觀承認入場優勢，並已在計分時充分補償。
B. 說話者認為勝者在入場前不可能有任何能力。
C. 比賽只看入場時間先後，並未評估競賽表現。
D. 這種唯才觀把入場前所需優勢，當成獲勝後才掙得的成就，令人質疑。
normal.explain: 揭露先備條件被追認為勝利應得的循環正當化。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
normal.speak: The memoir allows disappointment to remain disappointment, rather than conscripting it into an uplifting account of inevitable personal growth.
options: A. 回憶錄讓失望保有失望本身，不硬納入必然成長的勵志敘事。
B. 回憶錄主張失望已被後來成就證明毫無損失。
C. 作者否認任何人曾經因挫折而獲得成長。
D. 作者把每次失望都當成下一次勝利的可靠預兆。
normal.explain: 拒絕必然救贖框架，不否認有時成長。

normal.desc: 【語意】The victory was emphatic without being vindictive. What distinction is made?
options: A. The win was decisive, but not pursued or celebrated as revenge.
B. The win was narrow, but the celebrations were unusually prolonged.
C. The win was accidental, but the players claimed it as deserved.
D. The win was disputed, but the officials refused to review it.
normal.explain: emphatic 決定性明顯；vindictive 帶報復惡意。

normal.desc: 【文法】He would sooner ___ the point than win it through a disputed call.
options: A. to concede
B. concede
C. conceded
D. conceding
normal.explain: would sooner 後接原形；than 後 win 與之對應。

normal.desc: 【語用】The commentator calls the player remarkably selective in his respect for tradition after he invokes it only when it benefits him. What is implied?
options: A. His respect for tradition is strongest when it costs him an advantage.
B. His selective memory has made him forget every established practice.
C. His appeal to tradition is opportunistic rather than consistent.
D. His knowledge of tradition is unusually detailed and comprehensive.
normal.explain: selective 搭配只在有利時援引，諷刺原則隨利益選擇。

normal.desc: 【語域】Which reply declines to turn a sporting setback into a moral judgement about the player?
options: A. His good record means that the decision cannot properly be described as poor.
B. It was a poor decision under pressure, rather than evidence of poor character.
C. It tells us more about his character than any previous success ever could.
D. Pressure reveals character, so the decision settles what sort of person he is.
normal.explain: 正答承認差決定但拒絕概括人格；其他過度評斷或替決定開脫。

normal.desc: 【立場】The critic finds the celebration triumphalist rather than merely triumphant. What is criticised?
options: A. The uncertainty about whether the official result was final.
B. The decision to celebrate privately rather than with spectators.
C. The display of superiority over the defeated, beyond pleasure in winning.
D. The fact that the winners showed any pleasure in the result.
normal.explain: triumphalist 含炫耀優越、使敗者難堪意味，不只是 triumphant 勝利喜悅。

normal.desc: 【語意】The club’s egalitarian rhetoric sits uneasily with its deference to star players. What tension is identified?
options: A. Its equal treatment of players conflicts with the crowd’s preference for stars.
B. Its opposition to star status prevents any member from becoming well known.
C. Its preference for experienced members is openly stated as its guiding ideal.
D. Its language of equality conflicts with the special authority it grants some members.
normal.explain: 宣稱平等與實際對明星特殊服從有張力。

normal.desc: 【語用】The organisers insist that everyone is welcome, provided everyone can behave like the people already there. What is the criticism implicit in this formulation?
options: A. The welcome is limited solely by the physical capacity of the venue.
B. The group’s norms are being described as unknown to existing members.
C. The welcome may depend on conformity to an existing group’s norms.
D. The organisers have promised to revise norms for every newcomer.
normal.explain: 表面人人歡迎，實際以既有群體同化為條件。

normal.desc: 【短文】A club describes every demand for accommodation as special treatment while treating its existing arrangements as neutral. A member questions that neutrality. What is the strongest reading of the challenge?
options: A. Any existing arrangement is necessarily more unfair than a proposed alternative.
B. Accommodation can be assessed only after all existing members have left.
C. Special treatment is justified whenever a member uses that description.
D. Existing arrangements may already favour some needs, so neutrality itself needs examination.
normal.explain: 質疑預設的中立基準，不預先判斷所有新方案必優。

normal.desc: 【短文】The commentator attributes a win to character but a loss to circumstance. No reason is given for the different explanatory standards. What should a reader examine?
options: A. Whether favourable and unfavourable results are being explained asymmetrically.
B. Whether character can ever influence performance under difficult circumstances.
C. Whether the winning and losing matches followed exactly the same rules.
D. Whether the commentator had access to the official score before speaking.
normal.explain: 同一解釋標準是否因好壞結果而變，是核心問題。

normal.desc: 請唸出單字：面對壓力起伏仍保持平靜的心態
請唸出單字：無禮小氣而欠缺大方的
請唸出：對不同情況使用不對稱的判準
請唸出：帶偏向地訴諸公平的說法
請唸出：形式一致不能決定實質公平
normal.ans: FORMAL UNIFORMITY DOES NOT SETTLE SUBSTANTIVE FAIRNESS
normal.speak: formal uniformity does not settle substantive fairness
normal.vocabId: R8:FORMAL UNIFORMITY DOES NOT SETTLE SUBSTANTIVE FAIRNESS

normal.desc: 請唸出：冷靜接受不必表示沒有失望
normal.ans: CALM ACCEPTANCE NEED NOT IMPLY AN ABSENCE OF DISAPPOINTMENT
normal.speak: calm acceptance need not imply an absence of disappointment
normal.vocabId: R8:CALM ACCEPTANCE NEED NOT IMPLY AN ABSENCE OF DISAPPOINTMENT

normal.desc: 請拼出：對他人尤其對手寬宏大度的（M 開頭，11 個字母）
請拼出：令人蒙羞而不光彩的（I 開頭，11 個字母）
請拼出：對禮節或細節一絲不苟的（P 開頭，11 個字母）
填空題：E G A L I _ A R I A N (主張人人享有平等權利機會的)
填空題：P A _ T I _ A N (偏袒自己支持一方的)
填空題：S P _ C _ O _ S (貌似可信卻不成立的)
🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
options: A. 只修正標點而不改措辭
B. 重述時帶有偏向的改寫
C. 忠實保留所有限定的改寫
D. 為學習發音而逐字跟讀
normal.explain: tendentious 是為特定立場服務而偏頗。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
options: A. 不經思考而造成的混亂
B. 只有讀者知識不足才產生的誤會
C. 刻意維持的模稜兩可
D. 經研究後消除的歧義
normal.explain: studied 指經刻意設計，不是已研究消除。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
options: A. 經反覆驗證的最終結論
B. 公開拒絕接受的假設
C. 特意逐字引用的警告
D. 未明說而被預先當真的前提
normal.explain: presupposition 是預設，tacit 是未明說。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
options: A. 因缺乏資訊而明白承認不知道的聲明
B. 因術語複雜而需要專業解說的文件
C. 佯裝坦誠的免責聲明
D. 坦承全部責任而未保留的正式聲明
normal.explain: disingenuous 涉不坦誠的姿態，不只難讀。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
normal.speak: The disclaimer disowns an intention to mislead without addressing whether the presentation was misleading.
options: A. 聲明雖承認可能有誤導意圖，但保證未影響呈現。
B. 聲明已說明呈現不會誤導，卻保留是否故意的問題。
C. 聲明承認呈現有誤導效果，因此也承認原本意圖。
D. 聲明否認有意誤導，卻沒有回答呈現方式是否會造成誤導。
normal.explain: 動機與效果不同，否認前者未回答後者。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
normal.speak: The presenter’s neutrality consists in declining to state a preference, not in refraining from shaping the alternatives between which a preference can be expressed.
options: A. 主持人不明說自己偏好哪方，但仍影響哪些立場可供選擇。
B. 主持人雖公開支持一方，仍讓他人決定討論選項。
C. 主持人的中立既包括不表態，也包括不設定議題框架。
D. 主持人未表態，是因為來賓已先同意只有一種合理選項。
normal.explain: 不表態與不影響議題選項框架不同。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
normal.speak: The quotation acquires its insinuating force from the sentence beside it, which the defence of its literal accuracy conveniently ignores.
options: A. 影射來自引文本身的字詞錯誤，相鄰句已提供足以釐清的說明。
B. 辯護雖未強調字面正確，已充分承認相鄰句造成負面印象。
C. 說話者認為相鄰句改變了引文字詞，因此引文不再是逐字引用。
D. 引文因相鄰句而帶有影射，只強調逐字正確便略過這項脈絡。
normal.explain: 逐字真實與相鄰框架造成的暗示不同。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
normal.speak: The report does not so much silence the alternative view as admit it on terms that make it sound like a response to a question nobody sensible would ask.
options: A. 報告讓異見出現，卻用問題框架削弱它的合理性，而非直接禁聲。
B. 報告直接禁止異見者發言，再以主流意見代替他們可能提出的答案。
C. 報告承認異見同樣合理，但質疑讀者是否有足夠背景理解它。
D. 報告要求各方回答同樣合理的問題，只因異見答案較短而顯得薄弱。
normal.explain: 容納不等於公平呈現，框架仍可貶低異見的合理性。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
normal.speak: The headline’s certainty is not a faithful compression of the argument but a redistribution of its doubts to places a hurried reader is unlikely to reach.
options: A. 標題把疑慮放得比結論更顯眼，因此讀者容易低估論證的確定度。
B. 標題把保留疑慮移到匆忙讀者難以看到的地方，並非忠實濃縮論證。
C. 標題已完整交代疑慮，但讀者因匆忙閱讀而把它誤當成完全確定。
D. 疑慮經論證後已被排除，只是較後段文字尚未反映這個改變。
normal.explain: 資訊層級轉移保留，造成只讀醒目部分者高估確定性。

normal.desc: 【語意】The article is suggestive without being explicit. What characterises its method?
options: A. It gives exhaustive evidence before offering a conclusion.
B. It encourages an inference without stating it directly.
C. It states the accusation directly but supplies no evidence.
D. It avoids both implication and any identifiable subject.
normal.explain: suggestive 在此是暗示性，與 explicit 明說形成對比。

normal.desc: 【文法】Little ___ that her tentative remark would become the headline.
options: A. had anticipate she
B. she anticipated did
C. did she anticipate
D. she did anticipate
normal.explain: Little 前置表否定，引發 did + 主詞 + 原形倒裝。

normal.desc: 【語用】The editor calls the headline economical with the qualifications. The article contained several important caveats. What is the implication?
options: A. The headline has preserved each reservation in unusually concise language.
B. The headline’s shortness is being praised without any concern about meaning.
C. The article’s caveats have been rejected as too expensive to investigate.
D. The headline has omitted reservations that matter to its accuracy.
normal.explain: economical with qualifications 委婉諷刺省掉必要保留，不是成本。

normal.desc: 【範圍】The correction stops short of repudiating the inference drawn from the original claim. What remains?
options: A. The correction has been withdrawn from publication.
B. The inference has been replaced by a new allegation.
C. The inference has not been expressly disowned.
D. The original claim has been independently verified.
normal.explain: stops short of 表未做到某一步；未 repudiating 不等於證實。

normal.desc: 【語意】The interview’s ostensible openness is belied by the questions it makes impossible to ask. What is questioned?
options: A. Whether open questions are longer than questions requiring brief answers.
B. Whether the interviewer is willing to publish questions after the interview.
C. Whether an interview can be conducted without agreeing on a subject.
D. Whether an appearance of openness matches the permitted scope of discussion.
normal.explain: 公開姿態與可問範圍有落差；不是問題字數。

normal.desc: 【指涉】The statement denied that the omission was deliberate, not that it was consequential. Which position remains compatible?
options: A. The omission may have mattered even if it was accidental.
B. The omission was deliberate but did not affect the meaning.
C. The statement denied that any omission had occurred.
D. The statement accepted responsibility for every consequence.
normal.explain: 否定故意，不否定有影響；沒有明示完全承擔後果。

normal.desc: 【語用】The apology scrupulously expresses regret for the offence taken while remaining silent about the judgement that produced the offending remark. What distinction is exploited?
options: A. The speaker’s judgement is examined while the audience’s reaction is dismissed as irrelevant.
B. The offending remark is withdrawn while its public reception is described as favourable.
C. The audience’s interpretation is endorsed while the original remark is declared misquoted.
D. The audience’s reaction is acknowledged while the speaker’s underlying judgement escapes examination.
normal.explain: 遺憾停留於他人受冒犯，不觸及造成言論的自身判斷。

normal.desc: 【短文】A headline is softened after criticism, but the original wording survives in notifications already sent. The publisher calls the matter corrected. Which limitation should be examined?
options: A. Whether revising the page repairs the impressions created in channels the revision does not reach.
B. Whether notifications should contain every paragraph of an article before they can be distributed.
C. Whether the revised wording is less concise than the wording that originally attracted attention.
D. Whether readers who saw both versions can remember the exact time each notification arrived.
normal.explain: 修頁面不必觸及已發出的其他管道，修正效力有範圍。

normal.desc: 【短文】The interviewer asks when the guest stopped concealing the figures. The guest disputes having concealed them at all. Why is a direct date an inadequate response to the objection?
options: A. The interviewer has asked for a numerical estimate rather than a date.
B. Answering with a date would accept the contested presupposition.
C. Answering with a date would establish that the figures were never collected.
D. The objection concerns whether dates can be used in spoken interviews.
normal.explain: when stopped 預設曾隱瞞；客人挑戰的就是此預設。

normal.desc: 請唸出單字：以不直接方式提出的負面暗示
請唸出單字：明確拒絕接受或與之切割的表態
請唸出：刻意展現的坦誠姿態
請唸出：偽裝成問題的預設
normal.ans: A PRESUPPOSITION DISGUISED AS A QUESTION
normal.speak: a presupposition disguised as a question
normal.vocabId: R8:A PRESUPPOSITION DISGUISED AS A QUESTION

normal.desc: 請唸出：未表明偏好不必構成中立
normal.ans: AN ABSENCE OF STATED PREFERENCE NEED NOT CONSTITUTE NEUTRALITY
normal.speak: an absence of stated preference need not constitute neutrality
normal.vocabId: R8:AN ABSENCE OF STATED PREFERENCE NEED NOT CONSTITUTE NEUTRALITY

normal.desc: 請唸出：修正仍未充分檢視核心推論
normal.ans: THE CORRECTION LEAVES THE CENTRAL INFERENCE INSUFFICIENTLY EXAMINED
normal.speak: the correction leaves the central inference insufficiently examined
normal.vocabId: R8:THE CORRECTION LEAVES THE CENTRAL INFERENCE INSUFFICIENTLY EXAMINED

normal.desc: 請拼出：假裝坦誠或無知而實不誠懇的（D 開頭，12 個字母）
請拼出：以暗示方式傳達通常不利的意思（I 開頭，9 個字母）
請拼出：嚴格限制某事的範圍（C 開頭，12 個字母）
填空題：T E N D E _ T I O U S (為特定立場服務而偏頗的)
填空題：P R E S _ P P O S _ T I O N (未先證明便被當作成立的前提)
填空題：O B _ U S _ A T _ O N (使問題變得難以理解的混淆)
🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
options: A. 臨時借用但狀況完好的房間
B. 只在圖紙上存在的擴建方案
C. 建造或維護欠佳而搖搖欲墜的增建部分
D. 依原樣精細修復的附屬建築
normal.explain: ramshackle 指破舊不穩固，不只是非正式用途。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
options: A. 保留大量明顯磨損的室內
B. 尚未清空施工殘料的空間
C. 混合多種舊家具的室內
D. 未受破壞或髒污而如新的室內
normal.explain: pristine 指原始純淨或如新狀態，語境為室內狀況。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
options: A. 過分熱心干預他人事務的介入
B. 受明確委託且限於職責的協助
C. 沒有任何人注意到的偶然變化
D. 由所有住戶共同提出的需求
normal.explain: officious 指多管閒事，不等於 official 正式。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
options: A. 只願維護而不想擁有的態度
B. 對任何財物都不感興趣的態度
C. 主動邀請他人共同管理的態度
D. 把事物當成自己所有般的態度
normal.explain: proprietary 可描述彷彿有所有權的佔有心態。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
normal.speak: The room has the immaculate air of somewhere intended to be admired rather than inhabited.
options: A. 房間整潔得像供人欣賞而非生活。
B. 房間因日常使用痕跡而顯得比展示空間更有吸引力。
C. 房間雖供展示，設計者仍以居住舒適為首要考量。
D. 說話者認為房間凌亂失修，已不適合居住或參觀。
normal.explain: 反諷無瑕展示感與生活使用感的落差。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
normal.speak: His offer to organise the shelves would be more welcome if it did not carry the assumption that his idea of order must become everyone else’s.
options: A. 只要願意幫忙整理，就足以取得決定大家秩序觀的權利。
B. 若不預設他的秩序觀應由大家接受，整理提議會更受歡迎。
C. 大家其實接受他的秩序觀，只因整理工作太多而拒絕提議。
D. 提議不受歡迎，是因他拒絕提出任何具體整理方式。
normal.explain: 幫忙善意與強加個人標準有別，批評附帶預設。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
normal.speak: The redesign removes the signs of wear without quite considering that some residents regard them as signs of belonging.
options: A. 改造抹掉磨損痕跡，未充分考慮住戶可能視其為歸屬記憶。
B. 改造保留所有磨損，但未注意新住戶想要全新環境。
C. 住戶已一致同意磨損只代表疏於保養，沒有其他意義。
D. 改造者先取得住戶對歸屬感的共識，才決定保留磨損。
normal.explain: 同一痕跡可被讀為損耗或共同歷史，not quite 表未充分。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
normal.speak: The language of shared space does a remarkable amount of work in a proposal that gives one resident the final say over what everyone shares.
options: A. 說話者只批評共用空間的名稱太長，不涉及誰有決策權。
B. 提案高談共用，實際卻讓一人決定大家共用什麼。
C. 提案已把決策平均分配，所以共用一詞有充分實質根據。
D. 住戶先一致決定共用項目，才選一人執行已達成的共識。
normal.explain: remarkable amount of work 反諷修辭掩護實際權力不對等。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
normal.speak: One can question the sanctification of household routines without treating the disruption of those routines as an achievement in itself.
options: A. 說話者把任何打破慣例的行為都視為比維持更有價值。
B. 家務慣例因存在已久而不需接受任何實際效果的檢視。
C. 可質疑把家務慣例神聖化，也不必把破壞慣例本身當成成就。
D. 質疑家務慣例只有在立即提出全新慣例時才算合理。
normal.explain: 拒絕不可質疑與為反而反兩端，未要求即刻另立規則。

normal.desc: 【語意】The interior is immaculate but curiously inhospitable. What tension is conveyed?
options: A. An unfinished room is nevertheless ready for public use.
B. A crowded room has been mistaken for an empty one.
C. Faultless order coexists with a lack of welcome.
D. Visible wear coexists with an unusually warm atmosphere.
normal.explain: immaculate 無瑕整潔，inhospitable 不友善舒適；非物理髒亂。

normal.desc: 【文法】The room might have remained untouched, ___ not the residents insisted on keeping it in use.
options: A. were
B. should
C. did
D. had
normal.explain: had not the residents insisted ... 是 if residents had not insisted 的倒裝形式。

normal.desc: 【語用】Our belongings have apparently failed to meet the room’s new aesthetic standards, says a resident whose books were removed without consultation. What is implied?
options: A. A design preference has been allowed to override the resident’s say.
B. The resident has voluntarily agreed that the books should be discarded.
C. The books were moved solely because they were damaged beyond use.
D. The resident welcomes a neutral assessment of the books’ market value.
normal.explain: apparently 與擬人化 failed standards 反諷美學壓過協商權。

normal.desc: 【範圍】The renovation is not without merit, though its merits are not those advertised. What is conceded?
options: A. It has the advertised benefits, though fewer people recognise them.
B. It has no benefits, despite an effective advertising campaign.
C. Its benefits are apparent only to those who designed the advertisement.
D. It has benefits, but different ones from the claimed benefits.
normal.explain: 雙重否定承認有優點，後句區分實際與宣稱。

normal.desc: 【語意】The design aestheticises austerity while leaving the inconvenience to its occupants. What is criticised?
options: A. A visual ideal of spareness is pursued while users bear its practical costs.
B. A comfortable design is dismissed because it does not look sufficiently spare.
C. Occupants are choosing inconvenience in order to reduce the designer’s costs.
D. The design’s spare appearance disguises an unusually high level of comfort.
normal.explain: aestheticises 把簡樸美化，實際不便由使用者承擔。

normal.desc: 【指涉】The resident did not object to the shelves being moved so much as to not being asked. What is the principal objection?
options: A. The amount of time required to move the books.
B. The absence of consultation before the move.
C. The shelves’ new position relative to the window.
D. The person chosen to carry out the physical work.
normal.explain: not so much ... as ... 定位主不滿於程序而非結果。

normal.desc: 【語用】We have preserved its character, says the designer; You have preserved the part that photographs well, replies a resident. What is challenged?
options: A. The completeness of the designer’s account of what has been preserved.
B. The resident’s right to take photographs of the newly renovated room.
C. The claim that any original feature remains visible after the renovation.
D. The technical quality of the photographs used to document the project.
normal.explain: 回覆暗示保留偏重可展示視覺部分，質疑 character 被窄化。

normal.desc: 【短文】A room is called communal because nobody may personalise it. Residents consequently use it only for brief visits. A critic asks whether the policy protects shared ownership or merely prevents anyone from feeling at home. What is at issue?
options: A. Whether communal ownership requires each resident to receive an identical room.
B. Whether the restriction defeats part of the communal purpose it is meant to protect.
C. Whether short visits establish that the building has insufficient structural capacity.
D. Whether personal decoration should replace every rule governing communal use.
normal.explain: 保護共同空間的手段可能削弱歸屬感，是目的與手段張力。

normal.desc: 【立場】The essay declines to equate domestic order with moral worth, without denying that disorder can impose burdens on others. What balance is maintained?
options: A. It treats disorder as a moral failing whenever another person notices it.
B. It accepts order as the sole reliable measure of consideration for others.
C. It rejects a judgement of character while retaining concern for practical effects.
D. It rejects any shared standards because domestic habits are entirely private.
normal.explain: 不道德化個人，但保留對他人實際影響的責任考量。

normal.desc: 請唸出單字：破舊不穩固而欠維護的
請唸出單字：過分熱心而愛干涉他人事務的
請唸出：勉強作出的遷就安排
請唸出：與日常居住使用不協調的美學
normal.ans: AN AESTHETIC AT ODDS WITH HABITATION
normal.speak: an aesthetic at odds with habitation
normal.vocabId: R8:AN AESTHETIC AT ODDS WITH HABITATION

normal.desc: 請唸出：個人品味不應偽裝成中立標準
normal.ans: PERSONAL TASTE SHOULD NOT MASQUERADE AS A NEUTRAL STANDARD
normal.speak: personal taste should not masquerade as a neutral standard
normal.vocabId: R8:PERSONAL TASTE SHOULD NOT MASQUERADE AS A NEUTRAL STANDARD

normal.desc: 請唸出：可行折衷可能欠缺視覺一致
normal.ans: A WORKABLE COMPROMISE MAY LACK VISUAL UNIFORMITY
normal.speak: a workable compromise may lack visual uniformity
normal.vocabId: R8:A WORKABLE COMPROMISE MAY LACK VISUAL UNIFORMITY

normal.desc: 請拼出：年久或失修而破敗的（D 開頭，11 個字母）
請拼出：未受破壞髒污而如新的（P 開頭，8 個字母）
請拼出：不令人舒適或不友善的（I 開頭，12 個字母）
填空題：H A B I T _ T I O N (居住的行為或供人居住的狀態)
填空題：S A _ C T _ F Y (使某事被當成神聖不可質疑的)
填空題：A E S _ H E _ I C _ S E (以美學方式呈現或美化某事)
🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
options: A. 勉強收回的先前承諾
B. 精密計算後的最低付款
C. 尚未透露內容的邀請
D. 十分慷慨的提議
normal.explain: munificent 偏正式，指極慷慨。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
options: A. 走過場而不夠用心的諮詢
B. 反覆聽取並細查意見的程序
C. 因無人出席而完全未發生的會議
D. 私下向唯一專家取得的正式批准
normal.explain: perfunctory 指例行敷衍，不必會議未發生。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
options: A. 只比較兩張圖片尺寸的方法
B. 容易引起不滿而難堪的比較
C. 依共同尺度完成的中立測量
D. 為避免任何評價而作的描述
normal.explain: invidious 涉令人反感、引發嫉怨或不公平，非所有比較。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
options: A. 精心安排卻呈現自發感的效果
B. 沒有任何規劃的偶然互動
C. 只在舞蹈中才能出現的臨場動作
D. 因事前彩排不足而造成的混亂
normal.explain: choreographed 比喻編排；與 spontaneity 組成刻意張力。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
normal.speak: The invitation flatters its recipients as indispensable while making remarkably little provision for their being unavailable.
options: A. 說話者主要批評邀請沒有清楚列出活動場地。
B. 邀請稱受邀者不可或缺，卻少有為他們沒空作準備。
C. 邀請因預期受邀者沒空，已完整安排替補人選。
D. 受邀者因被認為可隨時替代，所以沒有收到邀請。
normal.explain: 奉承不可或缺與無備援的關係；未說確定誰不出席。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
normal.speak: What the audience experiences as seamlessness may be the point at which the workers’ improvisation becomes invisible.
options: A. 無縫順暢已證明活動從未需要臨場調整。
B. 說話者認為讓觀眾看見每項失誤是活動唯一目標。
C. 觀眾感到無縫順暢之處，可能正是工作人員應變被隱藏之處。
D. 觀眾看到明顯失誤，才會認為所有工作人員都沒有準備。
normal.explain: 順暢感可能由不可見的修補勞動支撐。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
normal.speak: The thank-you is gracious; whether it substitutes for the consultation that should have preceded the request is rather more doubtful.
options: A. 請求前已有完整諮詢，因此致謝反而顯得多餘。
B. 致謝很有禮，但能否代替請求前應有的諮詢很可疑。
C. 致謝不夠禮貌，所以先前諮詢內容也必定不可信。
D. 說話者確認只要充分感謝就不需事前徵詢。
normal.explain: 禮貌承認與事前知情同意的功能不同。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
normal.speak: The celebration of resilience is convenient for a plan that can remain unchanged only if the same people repeatedly absorb its deficiencies.
options: A. 說話者否認參與者在應付困難時展現任何能力。
B. 計畫維持不變是因參與者先共同決定不願作出修改。
C. 讚頌韌性讓計畫得以不改，代價是同些人反覆吸收缺陷。
D. 計畫已因大家的韌性改善，所以現在不再有任何缺陷。
normal.explain: 承認應變能力可能被用來免除改善計畫的責任。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
normal.speak: The programme’s informality is not an absence of structure so much as a structure whose demands are most legible to those already familiar with it.
options: A. 節目沒有結構，所以老參加者也無法理解任何要求。
B. 主辦者已把所有要求明列，新手與舊手同樣容易理解。
C. 說話者認為非正式活動應取消所有可能形成的規律。
D. 所謂非正式並非無結構，而是要求較易被熟悉它的人看懂。
normal.explain: 隱性結構可形成熟悉者優勢，非完全無規則。

normal.desc: 【語意】The event’s inclusiveness is conditional in ways its publicity leaves tactfully unspecified. What is suggested?
options: A. Its admission conditions are set out clearly but phrased with unusual politeness.
B. Its organisers have withdrawn the claim that anybody may attend.
C. Its publicity describes conditions that have not yet been approved.
D. Its welcome has limitations that promotional language avoids spelling out.
normal.explain: tactfully unspecified 帶批評暗示，有條件卻避談條件，非條件已清楚。

normal.desc: 【文法】However well ___, the invitation cannot supply the time its recipients lack.
options: A. intentioned
B. intending
C. has intended
D. was intending
normal.explain: well intentioned 是出於好意的形容詞組，省略 it is。

normal.desc: 【語用】The organiser says the extra work is entirely voluntary, then asks each person to explain publicly why they cannot do it. What tension arises?
options: A. Public explanations establish that everyone has the same amount of time.
B. Declining may carry social pressure despite the stated freedom.
C. The explanation requirement gives each person a confidential way to decline.
D. The extra work has been formally assigned only to those who volunteered.
normal.explain: 可拒絕的形式自由受公開自辯壓力削弱，未必形式強制。

normal.desc: 【範圍】The reviewer credits the improvisation without retrospectively dignifying the confusion that necessitated it. What is withheld?
options: A. Approval of the avoidable disorder preceding the recovery.
B. Recognition of the team’s skill in responding to the difficulty.
C. A claim that any improvisation took place during the event.
D. An account of why the participants appreciated the final result.
normal.explain: 肯定應變但不因此美化造成應變需求的混亂。

normal.desc: 【語意】The invitation’s munificence rests on an unexamined economy of other people’s time. What is criticised?
options: A. The event has failed because nobody is willing to devote any time to it.
B. Generosity to guests depends on labour whose costs are overlooked.
C. The guests are being charged for tasks they have already performed.
D. The organiser’s financial contribution has been exaggerated in the accounts.
normal.explain: 慷慨以他人未受檢視的時間成本為基礎；economy 不是只指帳務。

normal.desc: 【文法】The promise is one ___ fulfilment depends on people who were not consulted.
options: A. which its
B. that of
C. whose
D. whom
normal.explain: whose fulfilment 指承諾的實現；one 的所有格關係子句。

normal.desc: 【立場】The essay objects to the romanticisation of improvisation, not to improvisation as such. What is rejected?
options: A. Comparing the practical outcomes of planned and improvised arrangements.
B. Treating emergency adaptation as inherently admirable regardless of its causes or costs.
C. Allowing people to adapt plans when unexpected circumstances require a response.
D. Recognising that some successful activities include unscheduled contributions.
normal.explain: romanticisation 是浪漫美化，與應變本身有用與否不同。

normal.desc: 【短文】A festival claims to celebrate participation, yet credits only the people on stage and describes every supporting role as help. A volunteer questions the distinction. What is being examined?
options: A. Whether the festival should replace performances with a list of backstage tasks.
B. Whether all audience members ought to be assigned a formal volunteering role.
C. Whether the language of contribution makes some indispensable work appear peripheral.
D. Whether performing on stage requires exactly the same skills as supporting the event.
normal.explain: 命名與認可分配可能邊緣化必要工作，不要求角色完全相同。

normal.desc: 【短文】The plan assumes volunteers will cover any shortfall. Its apparent completeness therefore depends on leaving one category of work deliberately unquantified. What is the problem?
options: A. The plan’s detailed labour estimates prevent volunteers from choosing their roles.
B. The shortfall can be determined only after every volunteer has completed training.
C. The plan has counted voluntary labour twice in a published staffing total.
D. An unspecified reserve of labour conceals rather than resolves the planning gap.
normal.explain: 未量化人力被當無限補位，使缺口被遮掩而非已解決。

normal.desc: 請唸出單字：極其慷慨的給予或態度
請唸出單字：容易引起不滿嫉怨或顯得不公的
請唸出：將臨場應變美化的敘述
請唸出：由默示責任構成的交換運作方式
請唸出：形式自願不消除拒絕的社會代價
normal.ans: FORMAL VOLUNTARINESS DOES NOT ELIMINATE THE SOCIAL COST OF REFUSAL
normal.speak: formal voluntariness does not eliminate the social cost of refusal
normal.vocabId: R8:FORMAL VOLUNTARINESS DOES NOT ELIMINATE THE SOCIAL COST OF REFUSAL

normal.desc: 請唸出：不可見勞動能支撐輕鬆接待的表象
normal.ans: INVISIBLE LABOUR CAN SUSTAIN AN APPEARANCE OF EFFORTLESS HOSPITALITY
normal.speak: invisible labour can sustain an appearance of effortless hospitality
normal.vocabId: R8:INVISIBLE LABOUR CAN SUSTAIN AN APPEARANCE OF EFFORTLESS HOSPITALITY

normal.desc: 請拼出：收入或地位優厚而工作很少的閒職（S 開頭，8 個字母）
請拼出：出於自願而非被強迫的性質（V 開頭，13 個字母）
請拼出：用來使某人免責的（E 開頭，11 個字母）
填空題：M A G N A _ I M I T Y (對人寬厚大度的品格或行為)
填空題：R E C _ P R O _ I T Y (彼此相應給予或協助的互惠關係)
填空題：I N _ R D _ N _ T E (超出合理程度而過多的)
🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
options: A. 對逝去事物帶有哀思的語氣
B. 急於慶賀新成就的語氣
C. 只傳達計數而毫無情緒的口吻
D. 以命令要求立即行動的口吻
normal.explain: elegiac 偏文學，含哀悼追憶。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
options: A. 另加而用來模仿舊貌的裝飾
B. 先前事物留下的殘餘痕跡
C. 為未來改造預留的空白
D. 剛製成且從未使用的物件
normal.explain: residual 指殘存，不必出自刻意仿舊。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
options: A. 由作者公開標成虛構的小說
B. 因過於私密而從未流傳的紀錄
C. 真實性可疑卻常被傳述的軼事
D. 已經完整獨立證實的事蹟
normal.explain: apocryphal 指廣傳但可疑或不實，非明示創作小說。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
normal.speak: The object is genuine; the account of its arrival is the part that remains apocryphal.
options: A. 到來故事既流傳廣，物件就必定真實。
B. 物件真實，但其如何到來的故事仍真偽可疑。
C. 物件是仿品，但到來過程已完整證實。
D. 物件與來歷都已證明是同一人創作的小說。
normal.explain: 物件真偽與流傳故事真偽可分開。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
normal.speak: The label makes the absence of luxury sound like a virtue, without asking how much choice the owner had in the matter.
options: A. 標籤認為只有擁有奢侈物的人才具有美德。
B. 說話者只在比較收藏品目前的價格高低。
C. 標籤把沒有奢侈物說成美德，未問主人有多少選擇。
D. 主人自由拒絕奢華已獲證實，標籤只是轉述。
normal.explain: 自選節制與資源匱乏不同，評德需考慮選擇條件。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
normal.speak: The recollection is affectionate, but its affection seems to depend on keeping certain members of the household conveniently out of focus.
options: A. 回憶把每位家人都同樣清晰描述，因此特別溫情。
B. 照片因拍攝失焦而不能辨認，與敘事取捨無關。
C. 說話者認為記憶只要溫情就已證明其中人物虛構。
D. 回憶溫情，但似乎靠讓部分家人保持模糊而維持。
normal.explain: out of focus 比喻敘事邊緣化，seems 留推測。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
normal.speak: The catalogue is punctilious about dates and curiously incurious about whose work made those dates worth commemorating.
options: A. 日期既準確，目錄便已完整回答所有歷史問題。
B. 說話者只批評目錄沒有列出每件物品的重量。
C. 目錄仔細交代日期，卻不太追問誰的工作讓它們值得紀念。
D. 目錄詳細介紹工作者，卻把相關日期全部記錯。
normal.explain: 形式年代精確與勞動人物可見性不同。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
normal.speak: The universal appeal of the exhibit is purchased, in part, by stripping the object of the inconvenient specificity that made it someone’s possession rather than everyone’s metaphor.
options: A. 展品因完整保留每項人生差異，所以完全沒有共同聯想空間。
B. 物件原本由所有人共同持有，展覽後才被誤認為私人財產。
C. 說話者主要質疑展品售價太高，讓一般人無法購買。
D. 展品普遍吸引力部分來自抹去特定人生，讓私人物件變成人人的比喻。
normal.explain: purchase 為代價隱喻；普遍化可能犧牲具體歷史。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
normal.speak: One need not deny the comfort of nostalgia to question the retrospective tidiness with which it arranges lives that were considerably less tidy at the time.
options: A. 可承認懷舊慰藉，同時質疑它把當年紛亂人生事後整理得過於整齊。
B. 只要懷舊提供慰藉，當年人生就已被證明沒有紛亂。
C. 說話者否定懷舊的所有安慰作用，所以拒絕看舊物。
D. 當年家庭已非常整潔，回憶反而把它描述得過度混亂。
normal.explain: 情感功能與敘事理想化可分開檢視。

normal.desc: 【語意】The exhibition’s nostalgia is elegiac rather than celebratory. What tone predominates?
options: A. A reflective sadness for what has passed.
B. An exuberant welcome for what is about to begin.
C. A detached inventory with no emotional colouring.
D. An angry demand that every earlier custom return.
normal.explain: elegiac 挽歌式哀思，不等於激烈要求復古。

normal.desc: 【文法】The letter is all the more revealing for ___ intended for publication.
options: A. never being have
B. never having been
C. having never to be
D. not to have
normal.explain: for 後動名詞，never having been intended 表先前未打算公開。

normal.desc: 【語用】The label calls the owner a man of simple tastes beside a cabinet full of expensive curiosities. What does the juxtaposition invite?
options: A. Admiration for the owner’s refusal to collect any decorative objects.
B. A conclusion that simplicity can be measured by the cabinet’s dimensions.
C. Doubt about whether the flattering description fits the evidence.
D. Certainty that every object in the cabinet is a recent imitation.
normal.explain: 文字稱簡樸與昂貴珍奇櫃形成反諷落差，非必證假貨。

normal.desc: 【範圍】The memoir does not so much falsify the past as render its discomforts incidental to the story it wishes to tell. What is the criticism?
options: A. It refuses to select any details and therefore becomes unreadably long.
B. It subordinates awkward aspects rather than necessarily inventing events.
C. It openly invents every event while admitting none of it is historical.
D. It makes discomfort the central organising theme of the narrative.
normal.explain: not so much ... as ... 調整批評焦點到輕描淡寫與選擇框架。

normal.desc: 【修辭】The room is described as untouched by time, though the illusion requires daily maintenance. What paradox is exposed?
options: A. The maintenance proves that none of the displayed objects is old.
B. The description refers only to the absence of a clock in the room.
C. An appearance of timelessness depends on continuing intervention.
D. An untouched room necessarily requires less care than a renovated one.
normal.explain: 自然未變的表象其實靠持續工作維持，不否定物件年齡。

normal.desc: 【指涉】The curator disputes not the letter’s authenticity but its representativeness. What remains possible?
options: A. The letter is forged yet typical of the owner’s actual views.
B. The letter’s date is false but its handwriting is genuine.
C. The curator has rejected the existence of any wider correspondence.
D. The letter is genuine yet atypical of the wider correspondence.
normal.explain: 真實性與代表性不同，挑戰後者不必否定前者。

normal.desc: 【立場】The essay resists the fetishisation of the original without denying that a copy and an original have different histories. What balance is struck?
options: A. It refuses to display copies because originals deserve unquestioned reverence.
B. It makes visual similarity the only criterion of historical significance.
C. It questions automatic reverence while preserving a historical distinction.
D. It treats every copy as possessing exactly the same historical identity.
normal.explain: 不盲目崇原件，同時不抹平來源歷史差異。

normal.desc: 【短文】The display calls the worn handle evidence of generations of use, but describes a polished repair as damage to authenticity. No distinction is made between the intentions behind either alteration. What should be examined?
options: A. Whether every change to an object must be made by the same family member.
B. Whether a polished surface can ever reveal information about an object’s age.
C. Whether the worn handle and repaired surface belong to different exhibitions.
D. Why some changes acquire legitimacy as history while others are excluded from it.
normal.explain: 質疑歷史變動被選擇性認可的判準，不預先否定所有真實性區分。

normal.desc: 【語用】The visitor says, How fortunate that the family preserved exactly the things that make them look so generous. What is implied?
options: A. The surviving selection may favour a flattering account of the family.
B. The family’s generosity has been independently established by complete records.
C. Every surviving object must have been fabricated by a later collector.
D. The visitor wishes the family had sold the objects rather than preserved them.
normal.explain: 反諷選擇留存如何美化形象，未證實蓄意偽造。

normal.desc: 請唸出單字：大部分消失後留下的痕跡
請唸出單字：流傳卻真實性可疑的
請唸出：帶哀思追憶意味的回想
請唸出：未經檢視的重要性排序
請唸出：留存物反映選擇保存什麼的決定

normal.speak: a surviving object reflects decisions about what to preserve
normal.vocabId: R8:A SURVIVING OBJECT REFLECTS DECISIONS ABOUT WHAT TO PRESERVE

normal.desc: 請唸出：懷舊可安慰而未必準確重現過去
normal.ans: NOSTALGIA CAN COMFORT WITHOUT ACCURATELY RECOVERING THE PAST
normal.speak: nostalgia can comfort without accurately recovering the past
normal.vocabId: R8:NOSTALGIA CAN COMFORT WITHOUT ACCURATELY RECOVERING THE PAST

normal.desc: 請拼出：帶有挽歌式哀悼追憶情感的（E 開頭，7 個字母）
請拼出：存放聖物的容器，亦比喻珍藏遺物之處（R 開頭，9 個字母）
請拼出：將某物過度崇敬而忽略其脈絡的做法（F 開頭，13 個字母；字數依主要拼字，亦接受標準變體）
填空題：V E S T _ G I A L (僅殘存少量痕跡或原功能的)
填空題：E _ I _ E (在敘述中省略或略去)
填空題：I N _ I D _ N _ A L (附帶而非主要的)
🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
options: A. 完全不含立場的測量紀錄
B. 帶狡黠玩笑意味的評論
C. 只描述建築拱門的任何句子
D. 不顧語氣而直接發怒的指責
normal.explain: arch 描述知情而俏皮的口吻。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
options: A. 專門用來講解昆蟲的教材
B. 因沒聽清而重複提出的問題
C. 尖刻而帶刺的插話
D. 熱情鼓勵對方的正式致詞
normal.explain: waspish 比喻易怒尖酸，aside 插話。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
options: A. 不經意露出的驚訝表情
B. 因疼痛而產生的苦笑
C. 不願再與任何人交談的沉默
D. 刻意討好對方的微笑
normal.explain: ingratiating 指意圖獲人好感，可含負面做作。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
normal.speak: She congratulated him with a warmth that made his earlier attempts to belittle her look rather small.
options: A. 她只勉強道賀，所以他先前的批評顯得更有道理。
B. 她把祝賀改成批評，因此雙方繼續互相貶低。
C. 她熱情祝賀，使他先前貶低她的做法顯得小氣。
D. 她因祝賀而承認他先前貶低她完全合理。
normal.explain: warmth 與 belittle 對比，small 為小家子氣非體型。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
normal.speak: The narrator’s modesty has the curious effect of ensuring that every compliment eventually finds its way back to him.
options: A. 敘述者真誠拒絕每項讚美，從不談自己的貢獻。
B. 每項讚美因敘述者沉默而轉向其他人。
C. 說話者認為敘述者只是忘記誰曾讚美自己。
D. 敘述者的謙虛奇妙地讓每項讚美最後都回到自己。
normal.explain: 謙虛姿態可能為自我讚揚安排迂迴路徑。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
normal.speak: Her silence is not empty; it leaves him to supply the accusation she has tactfully refrained from making.
options: A. 她的沉默不是沒意思，而是讓他自己補出她未明說的指責。
B. 她沉默因不知發生何事，所以請他提供全部資訊。
C. 她已明白說出指責，他只需逐字重複。
D. 沉默已證明她同意他先前每項辯解。
normal.explain: 不明說仍可引發內疚或預設指責，不斷言她真的掌握證據。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
normal.speak: The anecdote is ostensibly at his own expense, though he emerges from it looking remarkably considerate.
options: A. 軼事直接承認自己不體貼，沒有任何自我美化。
B. 故事由別人付錢出版，因此他沒付任何成本。
C. 說話者主要關心講故事的人是否收到出場費。
D. 軼事表面拿自己開玩笑，結果卻顯得自己格外體貼。
normal.explain: at own expense 在此自嘲，ostensibly 暗示實際自我稱許。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
normal.speak: The scene’s comedy lies in the discrepancy between the freedom the host ceremoniously grants and the gratitude with which he expects it to be returned unused.
options: A. 喜劇落差在主人隆重給自由，卻期待客人感謝並不去用它。
B. 主人真正希望客人用自由作任何決定，只要求事後告知。
C. 客人已明確要求取消自由，主人卻拒絕接受。
D. 場景只嘲笑主人說話太慢，與實際選擇無關。
normal.explain: grants/returned unused 揭露形式大方與實際期待矛盾。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
normal.speak: The narrator does not quite lie; he merely arranges the facts so that the most flattering explanation seems to arrive without his assistance.
options: A. 說話者認為只要沒有明說謊言，任何選材都必然公正。
B. 敘述者未必說謊，只安排事實讓最有利自身的解釋看似自然出現。
C. 敘述者直接捏造全部事實，並明言自己在創作虛構。
D. 最有利他的解釋已由外人獨立查證，與敘事安排無關。
normal.explain: 選材可引導讀者，未必需要逐項造假。

normal.desc: 【語意】The narrator’s self-deprecation is oddly self-congratulatory. What tension is conveyed?
options: A. His criticism of himself leaves no room for any sense of achievement.
B. His apparent modesty becomes a way of praising himself.
C. His praise of others prevents him from discussing himself.
D. His modesty is consistently unnoticed by every other character.
normal.explain: 自嘲姿態反而彰顯自身優點，是看似謙虛實則自誇。

normal.desc: 【文法】Such ___ the delicacy of the subject that even the silence seemed tactless.
options: A. had
B. being
C. was
D. were
normal.explain: Such was + 單數名詞組 + that ...，表程度結果。

normal.desc: 【語用】He was, she assured us, entirely free to decide, provided he arrived at the decision she had already announced. What is exposed?
options: A. The decision has genuinely been delegated without any expectation about the result.
B. The speaker has changed her mind because he refuses to accept her advice.
C. The group has agreed to postpone announcing a decision until he returns.
D. The purported freedom is emptied by a predetermined acceptable outcome.
normal.explain: 表面自由附帶只能選既定答案的條件，形成反諷。

normal.desc: 【範圍】The portrait is unsparing without being gratuitously cruel. What distinction is maintained?
options: A. It invents faults in order to make the person appear admirable.
B. It excuses needless hurt whenever the description is entertaining.
C. It exposes faults frankly without inflicting needless hurt.
D. It avoids any fault that might upset the person portrayed.
normal.explain: unsparing 不留情揭短；否認 gratuitously cruel 無故殘酷。

normal.desc: 【短文】A character rehearses a spontaneous apology several times, then criticises his companion for failing to respond naturally. What contradiction structures the scene?
options: A. He prefers a written apology because his companion cannot hear him clearly.
B. His companion has rehearsed the apology without telling him about it.
C. He has forgotten the words and therefore cannot make any apology.
D. He demands an unplanned response to an encounter he has carefully scripted.
normal.explain: 自發要求與自編劇本形成矛盾，不是單純忘詞。

normal.desc: 【語意】The narrator’s solicitude shades into proprietorial concern. What shift is suggested?
options: A. Care begins to resemble a claim to control.
B. Concern gradually gives way to complete indifference.
C. Fear about property replaces interest in another person’s feelings.
D. The narrator stops caring because the property has been sold.
normal.explain: solicitude 關心，proprietorial 帶佔有/主控，shades into 漸變。

normal.desc: 【語用】The guest was welcomed so elaborately that declining the invitation became a public performance. What is implied?
options: A. The guest has requested a theatrical role as part of the event.
B. The invitation has been withdrawn before the guest can respond.
C. The host has made a private refusal easier by keeping it confidential.
D. The welcome makes a nominally free refusal socially difficult.
normal.explain: 過度歡迎增加拒絕的公開壓力，未定為正式強迫。

normal.desc: 【短文】The narrator describes himself as the only person who understood the quarrel, yet quotes each participant only where their words support his own grievance. What should a reader scrutinise?
options: A. The selection through which his claim to superior understanding is constructed.
B. Whether understanding a quarrel requires never having a personal grievance.
C. Whether every participant used the exact same vocabulary during the argument.
D. The possibility that any quotation can preserve the wording of spoken speech.
normal.explain: 優越理解可能由偏向選材建立，非因有怨即不可能理解。

normal.desc: 【修辭】The hostess’s tact is described as leaving every awkward subject untouched and everyone acutely aware of its location. What is the effect?
options: A. The physical arrangement of the room prevents private conversation.
B. Avoidance paradoxically makes the subjects more conspicuous.
C. The narrator confirms that nobody knows what the subjects are.
D. Tact has resolved the disagreement by making the subjects irrelevant.
normal.explain: untouched/location 隱喻避談反使禁區顯眼。

normal.desc: 請唸出單字：對他人的殷切關心
請唸出單字：尖刻易怒而帶刺的
請唸出：試圖討好他人的態度
請唸出：對他人帶有佔有意味的關心
normal.ans: A PROPRIETORIAL CONCERN FOR ANOTHER PERSON
normal.speak: a proprietorial concern for another person
normal.vocabId: R8:A PROPRIETORIAL CONCERN FOR ANOTHER PERSON

normal.desc: 請唸出：和解仍可能留下部分不信任
normal.ans: A RECONCILIATION MAY LEAVE SOME DISTRUST INTACT
normal.speak: a reconciliation may leave some distrust intact
normal.vocabId: R8:A RECONCILIATION MAY LEAVE SOME DISTRUST INTACT

normal.desc: 請唸出：他表面謙虛確保讚美回到自己
normal.ans: HIS APPARENT MODESTY ENSURES THAT THE PRAISE RETURNS TO HIM
normal.speak: his apparent modesty ensures that the praise returns to him
normal.vocabId: R8:HIS APPARENT MODESTY ENSURES THAT THE PRAISE RETURNS TO HIM

normal.desc: 請拼出：刻意討好以獲人好感的（I 開頭，12 個字母）
請拼出：對現狀自滿而缺少警覺的心態（C 開頭，11 個字母）
請拼出：顯示把事物或他人當成自己所有的（P 開頭，13 個字母）
填空題：A R _ H (故作狡黠而帶玩笑意味的)
填空題：T A _ T L _ S S (未顧及他人感受而不得體的)
填空題：F E _ I C _ T _ U S (措辭或行動貼切而巧妙的)
🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
options: A. 讓每個人任選標準的建議
B. 沒有任何條件的正式許可
C. 規定應如何達成要求的規格
D. 只記錄已發生狀況的摘要
normal.explain: prescriptive 有規範應然性，非純描述。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
options: A. 由定義保證永遠成立的定理
B. 刻意設計得無法理解的暗號
C. 已被證明矛盾的每項結論
D. 可因新資訊而被推翻的假設
normal.explain: defeasible 指可被足夠反證推翻，不等於已推翻。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
options: A. 可用具體操作判斷是否符合的標準
B. 只以抽象稱讚而不提供判斷方式
C. 只能由詞源而不能由行動理解的名稱
D. 不論結果如何都無法檢驗的立場
normal.explain: operational criterion 需可實際用於判斷，不只漂亮用語。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
normal.speak: The example is meant to disambiguate the instruction, not introduce a second requirement that the text never states.
options: A. 範例有意取代文字，所以未寫要求一律以圖為準。
B. 文字已完整列出第二要求，範例只是重複它。
C. 說話者認為只要例子與文字同時存在，就必定矛盾。
D. 範例用來釐清指示，不是新增文字未提的另一要求。
normal.explain: 解釋範例功能不等於無限制加條件。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
normal.speak: The instruction is unambiguous once one has already decided which of its two possible readings the author intended.
options: A. 先決定作者要哪種讀法才不歧義，這其實沒解決原有歧義。
B. 指示本身已排除第二種讀法，不需任何意圖判斷。
C. 作者已明示兩種讀法都可用，所以不再有選擇問題。
D. 說話者只在說不同字體會使人看不清文字。
normal.explain: 帶反諷的循環條件，需先解歧才能說無歧。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
normal.speak: A tolerance is meaningful only in relation to the function it protects; describing a deviation as small does not establish that it is harmless.
options: A. 說話者認為每個微小偏差都必定造成嚴重損壞。
B. 容差要對照保護的功能，偏離數字小不保證影響無害。
C. 只要偏差數字小，就不需要再看物件實際用途。
D. 功能已確定不受影響，所以任何容差都應取消。
normal.explain: 相對功能判斷，拒絕無條件小即無害，也不說小必有害。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
normal.speak: The result may vindicate the choice in this instance without establishing a rule that the same choice will serve every instance.
options: A. 這次結果可支持此選擇，未證明每次都同樣適用。
B. 這次結果已建立普遍規則，之後不必看任何條件。
C. 說話者因單次成功而認為選擇反倒不值得採用。
D. 相同選擇已在每種情況逐一獨立試驗成功。
normal.explain: 單例成效與普遍外推不同，保留有限支持。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
normal.speak: The apparent simplicity comes from omitting the decisions an experienced maker supplies automatically; it is not necessarily a property a novice can inherit by reading the same page.
options: A. 說話者認為新手永遠不可能透過指示學到任何技能。
B. 表面簡單靠熟手自動補足決策，新手讀同頁未必同樣容易。
C. 熟手與新手只要讀相同頁，就會自動具備相同判斷。
D. 說明已把所有決策完整寫出，只是熟手讀得較慢。
normal.explain: 熟練者內隱補足不可直接外推新手，同時不否認可學習。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
normal.speak: The exception is framed as though it merely clarifies the rule, yet it removes precisely the cases in which compliance would test the rule’s adequacy.
options: A. 規則本來沒有任何適用案例，例外才讓它開始可用。
B. 說話者只質疑例外句子比主規則句子更長。
C. 例外看似只釐清規則，卻排除最能檢驗規則是否足夠的案例。
D. 例外增加最困難案例，所以規則受到更嚴格測試。
normal.explain: 排例外可能讓規則免於關鍵反證，未說所有例外不合理。

normal.desc: 【語意】The instruction is permissive about materials but prescriptive about sequence. What follows?
options: A. Both materials and sequence must follow the example exactly.
B. Neither materials nor sequence has any bearing on the result.
C. Materials may vary, while the order of steps is constrained.
D. Materials are fixed, while the order of steps is left open.
normal.explain: permissive 容許變通，prescriptive 規定應做方式；適用不同面向。

normal.desc: 【文法】The instruction is no clearer for ___ repeated in a larger font.
options: A. to be
B. been
C. it being has
D. being
normal.explain: for 後動名詞，no clearer for being repeated 表重複未改善清晰。

normal.desc: 【範圍】A component may be replaced only if both dimensions remain within tolerance. Which interpretation is warranted?
options: A. Acceptable dimensions are necessary for replacement, not necessarily sufficient.
B. Acceptable dimensions guarantee that replacement is required.
C. One acceptable dimension is sufficient even if the other falls outside tolerance.
D. Replacement is prohibited whenever both dimensions satisfy the stated limits.
normal.explain: only if 設必要條件，both 要兩者；未排除其他必要要求。

normal.desc: 【語用】The manual is admirably exact about what to do once the preliminary arrangements are complete, and serenely silent about how to complete them. What is implied?
options: A. Its silence confirms that the preliminary arrangements require no work.
B. Its exactness makes any preliminary arrangement unnecessary.
C. Its preliminary section is more detailed than its main instructions.
D. Its procedural precision leaves an important prerequisite unexplained.
normal.explain: 反諷精細主流程卻略過前提如何達成。

normal.desc: 【語意】The diagram gains simplicity by omitting information about reversibility: its arrows no longer show which steps can be undone. What is sacrificed?
options: A. Information about whether earlier operations can be reversed.
B. The ability to reverse the physical direction in which the page is held.
C. Evidence that every operation should be performed twice.
D. The distinction between written instructions and printed arrows.
normal.explain: economy 簡化代價在可逆性資訊，非紙可否旋轉。

normal.desc: 【指涉】The warning qualifies the permission, not the obligation. What should a reader examine?
options: A. Whether permission and obligation have been defined as identical.
B. The conditions under which an allowed action may be taken.
C. The conditions under which a required action may be ignored.
D. Whether the warning withdraws every earlier requirement.
normal.explain: permission 允許，obligation 義務；限定許可不等於豁免義務。

normal.desc: 【立場】The critic does not demand exhaustive instructions, but objects to presenting omissions as though they were freedoms deliberately granted to the user. What is challenged?
options: A. The rebranding of insufficient guidance as intentional flexibility.
B. The possibility that concise instructions can be useful to an experienced user.
C. The user’s right to choose between more than one acceptable method.
D. The inclusion of any example that omits irrelevant decorative details.
normal.explain: 資訊缺漏被美化成自由，非要求全部百科式說明。

normal.desc: 【短文】A procedure says any suitable material may be used, then defines suitable as whatever makes the procedure work. It offers no test available before the attempt. What is the practical limitation?
options: A. The procedure prevents users from evaluating the outcome after making an attempt.
B. The criterion does not guide selection independently of the outcome it is meant to secure.
C. The procedure establishes that every available material will produce the same result.
D. The criterion excludes materials solely because they have not been used previously.
normal.explain: 適合與成功循環定義，無法事前選材；非不能事後評估。

normal.desc: 【短文】A manual instructs users to preserve the original orientation while reversing the assembly. It does not specify whether reversing means undoing the steps or turning the object over. What needs clarifying?
options: A. Whether the assembly contains the same number of parts as the illustration.
B. Which brand of material is recommended for a more durable result.
C. Which sense of reversing is intended and how it relates to orientation.
D. Whether original refers to the first printed edition of the manual.
normal.explain: 多義動詞與朝向指示有歧義，應先區分操作反做與翻轉。

請唸出單字：可能被進一步資訊推翻的
請唸出：實際操作上有意義的區分
請唸出：未明確說出的先決條件
請唸出：條件達成不會把許可變成義務

normal.speak: permission does not become obligation when its condition is met
